title: Catching lab (protocol E.2 / section 6)
_source: ralph/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md E.2, transcribed mechanically per ralph/GATE_F_INSTRUMENTATION_REQUEST.md section 6. Entry saves per protocol B: S05-exit (band 1 field) and S08-exit (party of 5).
_lane: SEGMENT_SCHEMA.md lists `journey` and `diag` as the lane values. This segment is neither: protocol 0.1 names two lanes, JOURNEY (S01-S10) and STUDY/DIAG (X01-X08), and only the segments prefixed DIAG- inside that second lane may take a shortcut. `study` is that distinction written down rather than collapsed into `diag`, which would read as permission this segment does not have. The field is informational either way -- the per-step `diag` flag is what actually permits a shortcut, and no step here carries one.
_config: E.2's own catch config reference: data/config/catching.json -- throw speed 17, gravity 14, max flight 4 s, cooldown 0.9 s; orbs basic/greater/prime; D31 explicit percent.
_per_throw: E.2's per-throw record, which every throw below feeds: aim time, throw count, distance, target species/size, hit/miss and stated reason, shown percent, result, party count after, feedback observed, camera behavior during aim/throw/resolve.
_hard_rules: A trainer-owned creature CANNOT be caught and the party maximum is five with no storage and no sixth slot (CLAUDE.md). CT-06 and CT-09 are transcribed as expected REFUSALS and as a five-slot presentation check, never as expected successes.
_no_teleport: X03 is not a DIAG segment and contains no teleport step.
_shot_ids: Protocol G defines the catch family open-endedly as 'GF-15-CATCH-01...n | aim reticle frame + resolve frame per CT class'. The numbering used here keys the shot to the CT case and uses the a/b pair protocol G already uses for GF-22 defect shots: GF-15-CATCH-<nn>a is the aim reticle frame and GF-15-CATCH-<nn>b the resolve frame for case CT-<nn>. CT-01's pair (01a/01b) therefore belongs to the journey's S02, and X03 takes 02 onward.
_comment_evidence_lane: §H/§G evidence split, owner decision 2026-08-27, recorded in ralph/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md §H.1. This is the LOGIC lane: the journey run headless for mechanics, telemetry and step verdicts at 6.1 ms/frame against 12,721 ms for a rendered frame on the Gate F container. It takes no prescribed frame; the §G ids its steps would have taken are DELEGATED to X03C, which declares each of them in its "owes" list. The harness refuses to start this segment if X03C does not exist, does not declare evidence_lane=capture, or does not accept every id handed to it -- a delegation nobody accepted is a debt that has quietly stopped existing, which is the same shape as the 9,231 file:null PASSes CD-1 was written for. Whether the debt was actually PAID is a question about the whole run directory and is answered by tools/gate_f/run_inventory.py, not here.
_comment_record_hz_split: AMENDED for the §H/§G evidence split. record_hz is forced to 0 on a logic lane by the harness regardless of what this file says, because §H's continuous record is the thing the split removes: the recorder's cadence is counted in PLAY seconds now, but under a 12.7 s rendered frame even a 0.1 Hz record fires on every rendered frame, and the eighteen segments' 4,607,802 physics frames are ~8,283 hours. The obligation is not dropped -- §H's prescribed frames move to X03C, which may run BOUNDED record windows around a named state.

steps.title: AMBIGUITY: which GF-19 shot CT-08 means

args.text: CT-08's evidence column says 'telemetry + GF-19 shot'. The only GF-19 frame about party slots is GF-19-UI-09, 'party strip at 5/5', and protocol L.4 sites that one in segment S08: 'HUD: five slots max, no sixth implied | GF-19-09 at 5/5 party | S08 | shot'. CT-08 is a party-NOT-full case, so GF-19-UI-09 cannot honestly be taken here either. No shot is invented: the count and the slot presentation are recorded in telemetry and this note names the gap.

steps.expected: a note event carries this observation into events.jsonl

steps.title: AMBIGUITY: what the party count is at S05-exit

args.text: CT-08 needs a party that is not full, and the protocol never says how many creatures S05-exit holds -- protocol B's span for S03 is 'team of 3' and nothing fixes the count at S05. The two asserts below are written as 4 then 5, so that 'party count increments' is a real verdict rather than an unfalsifiable one. A FAIL on the first of them is a bookkeeping mismatch about the entry save, not a game defect, and the event's own `party` field carries the true count either way.
